chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Hariz ibn Abdillah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who gave another man the funds for a Hajj to perform on his behalf from Kufa, but he performed it from Basra. He said: 'There is no harm if he fulfilled all the rituals, for his Hajj is complete.'
And whoever gave another man the funds for a Hajj al-ifrad, and he performed Hajj al-tamattu' on his behalf, that is sufficient for him. Narrated.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمَنَاسِكَ: The rituals and rites of Hajj
key_terms.حَجَّةٌ: Funds or money allocated for performing Hajj
key_terms.حَجُّ التَّمَتُّعِ: A type of Hajj where the pilgrim performs Umrah first, exits Ihram, and then enters Ihram again for Hajj
key_terms.حَجُّ الِافْرَادِ: A type of Hajj where the pilgrim remains in the state of Ihram from Miqat until the end, without performing Umrah first

ai.seo_question: Is Hajj valid if the pilgrim uses the provided funds to perform a different type of Hajj or in a different city?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the flexibility of Hajj validity regarding the donor's intent versus the pilgrim's actual performance, a key issue in Shia fiqh concerning *Hajj al-Tamatt'* and *Hajj al-Qiran*. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that the essential condition is the completion of all rituals (*manasik*), rendering the specific city of departure or the type of Hajj performed secondary to the core obligation. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the substantive fulfillment of rites over rigid adherence to the donor's initial specification, provided the pilgrim executes the required acts correctly.
